text:
sasha: Heads up — since the kernel-selector v2 rollout at ~03:00 UTC, we're seeing a regression in token-level tail latency and KV prefix cache behavior. Spike in evictions and much lower reuse_by_route.

ryan: ugh, saw p99 increase on the alert board. Which routes are most affected?

sasha: /chat/compose is the worst — prefix_cache hit_rate dropped from ~0.92 -> ~0.63 there. Evictions/sec jumped ~4x. Node-level memory footprint for the kvcache process on node-gpu-12 jumped 48GB -> 72GB after the roll. Quick PromQL I used: 
```
sum by(route) (rate(prefix_cache_evictions_total[5m]))
sum by(route) (prefix_cache_hits_total) / sum by(route) (prefix_cache_requests_total)
```

maya: @sasha can you paste the grafana panel? Also did batching-heuristic alpha land at the same time?

sasha: grafana: https://grafana.redwood/e/abc123/kvcache-heatmap (link). Yes — batching-heuristic alpha toggle + kernel-selector now prefers fused-attention kernels for seq_len 1..512.

elaine: Curious if fused kernels change memory layout and increase KV bookkeeping churn. Could be more allocations or misaligned buffers causing premature evictions.

ryan: remember the KV-shard sizing bug we fixed earlier? If the fused path uses a different handle lifecycle it could fail to pin prefixes and cause reuse to drop.

sasha: I ran a quick perf on a canary request and saw ~18% cycles in memcpy during "prefix reconstruction" in the kernel-selector path. Flame shows KV-related memcpy + small allocs. Will attach pprof later.

infra-bot: canary-deploy: kernel-selector-v2 rolled to 40% at 03:00 UTC — health checks OK.

maya: Proposed plan: 1) revert kernel-selector on canary, 2) collect slow traces for /chat/compose + /embed routes, 3) run per-route sampling to compute reuse_by_route distribution and heatmap. Who owns?

ryan: I'll revert canary now and collect perf traces and jemalloc stats. Starting revert.

sasha: Also adding temporary dashboard panels: "kv_prefix_cache: reuse_by_route (sampled 5m)" and "evictions/sec per node". Will open a PR for the panels.

elaine: We should also split token-level latency into finer spans: token_decode + kv_lookup + kernel_select + kernel_exec. Current tracing only reports decode + total which hides KV cost.

maya: Good call — I'll add spans for kv_lookup and kernel_select in runtime traces and update the trace schema. Quick PromQL to get token-level buckets per route: 
```
sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route)
```

ryan: Revert completed at ~03:50 UTC. Canaries show evictions down ~70% and reuse_by_route trending back up. Collecting perf traces and saving to s3: s3://perf-dumps/1830123456-canary-traces.tar.gz

sasha: Great. Follow-ups: file a perf-regression ticket referencing kernel-selector v2, add a unit test for KV lifetime in fused-kernel path, and add an alert: route-level prefix_cache_hit_rate < 0.8 for 10m -> paging.

maya: I'll create the ticket (ENG-9573) and add the alert rule. Also will coordinate a targeted benchmark to measure token-level breakdown across kernel variants.

ryan: attaching short trace snippet and jemalloc stats in the ticket. I'll also run a controlled workload to reproduce on a staging fleet.

sasha: thx all. Moving dashboard PR to review and will post results from sampled traces here when available. :mag_right:
